name: crewdson-terrace-blue-hour
prompt: Tall portrait frame, camera at chest height in the middle of an ordinary British terraced street just after sunset, looking straight down the road with a slight upward tilt. Two rows of red-brick two-up two-down houses run away on either side, front doors opening onto the pavement, green and black wheelie bins lined up by the low walls, small hatchbacks parked nose to tail along both kerbs, net curtains glowing amber in a few front rooms. Planted in the centre of the tarmac, filling the upper two thirds of the frame, is a single enormous stack of plain white paper reaching as high as the chimney pots, its sheets slightly uneven at the edges like a ream grown to the size of a building. Across the thick edge of the topmost sheets, in large black capital letters, it reads "THE RULES". In the lower third, small against it, five people stand in a loose uneven line with their backs half turned to us, heads tipped back, looking up at the stack. They wear present-day clothes: a puffer jacket, a grey hoodie under a parka, a tracksuit top, a work fleece, a rain mac, trainers and jeans. Every one of them wears a knitted balaclava, each a different colour (charcoal, navy, olive, maroon, black), covering the whole head with no openings for eyes, nose or mouth, a thick white ring stitched around the face and a solid red triangle stitched high inside the ring over the wearer's left eye, so on the two figures turned towards camera it sits to the right of the picture near two o'clock, not centred. Hems of the balaclavas tuck into their collars, both hands in dark gloves, sleeves pulled over the wrists, no skin visible anywhere, no metal or lights on the masks, just cloth. The light is deliberate and staged: orange sodium streetlamps pool on the wet tarmac, warm window light spills onto the bins and car roofs, a car's interior light is on, and one hard cold white beam from low and off to the side rakes up the face of the paper stack, picking out every layered sheet edge and the printed words in crisp detail. Above the rooftops the sky is a deep saturated cobalt blue with no stars. The rest of the street is warm amber against that blue. Still, silent, uncanny, nobody else around, the air very slightly hazy. Deep focus with the stack pin sharp, photographic realism, medium-format film texture, fine grain, no text other than THE RULES.
